name: Run payroll
summary: Every two weeks the payroll team pays about 1,300 employees, a third of them unionised plant, mine and field workers on rotating shifts whose pay includes shift, weekend, call-out and double-time overtime premiums. Supervisors approve their crews' time, payroll imports and checks it against collective agreement rules, enters HR changes, reviews the register and sends the direct deposit file two banking days before pay day. After pay day the team remits source deductions to the CRA on the accelerated schedule, pays union dues and posts labour costs to work orders and projects. Late timesheet approvals, premium coding errors and retroactive pay after late bargaining settlements cause most of the rework.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant power generator with about 1,300 employees under 11 collective agreements, a time and attendance system feeding an HR and payroll system, and a six-person payroll team in human resources.
baseline.notes: In-house payroll on a commercial HR and payroll system, biweekly for all staff; no outsourced payroll bureau assumed.

trigger: The biweekly pay period ends and time and attendance locks the period.
end_state: Net pay is deposited, statements are published, source deductions and dues are remitted, and labour costs are posted and reconciled in the general ledger.

volume.seasonality: 26 regular runs a year, so two months a year have three runs; off-cycle bonus runs in March and severance runs during the 2021 mine closure.

evidence.note: Kept from the organisation file; biweekly pay is stated in the process description.

Organisation file lists 6 payroll specialists. About 2 FTE goes to the biweekly run itself; the rest goes to benefits and pension administration, records of employment, garnishment setup, year-end slips and employee questions outside the run. Estimate.

Stands for all front-line supervisors who approve crew time (plant shift supervisors, maintenance, hydro, wind, mine and specialist crew supervisors, about 60 people). Shift, weekend and overtime premiums under the IBEW agreement (hrr_ibew254) must be coded on each timesheet. About 20 minutes per supervisor per run is an estimate.
Approves each payroll register and funding total. Estimate.
Funds the payroll account and approves the bank file. Estimate.
Reconciles payroll clearing and liability accounts after each run. Estimate.

systems.name: ERP (finance, purchasing and plant maintenance modules)
Bank cash management portal (direct deposit file and CRA remittance)

steps.name: Close pay period in time and attendance
steps.description: At the end of the biweekly pay period the time and attendance system locks the period, fills scheduled hours for shift workers from their rotation and lists timesheets that still have missing punches, unapproved overtime or unexplained absences.

evidence.note: Biweekly pay periods are given in the organisation file process description; schedule-driven time capture for rotating shifts was the common setup.

steps.name: Approve crew timesheets and code exceptions
steps.description: Each front-line supervisor opens the timesheets for their crew, adds overtime, call-outs, shift trades, standby and acting-up pay with the right premium codes from the collective agreement, checks them against the shift log and approves them before the payroll deadline, usually the first working morning after the period ends.

error.defect_description: Overtime, call-out or shift premium coded wrongly or not at all.

control.basis: Supervisor approval of hours worked; pay codes defined by the collective agreements

evidence.note: Touch is the combined time of about 60 supervisors who work in parallel, so it overstates elapsed time. Premium types come from the IBEW Local 254 agreement summary; timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Chase missing timesheet approvals
steps.description: The payroll specialist runs the unapproved-timesheet report, emails or phones supervisors and their backups for the missing approvals, and for crews whose supervisor is off rotation asks the plant manager to approve.

evidence.note: Some approvals are missing every run because supervisors rotate off shift. Estimate.

steps.name: Import approved time into payroll
steps.description: The payroll specialist runs the interface that sends approved hours and pay codes from time and attendance to the HR and payroll system, and checks that the record count and total hours agree between the two systems.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Clear interface rejects and premium flags
steps.description: The payroll specialist works through the error report: invalid pay codes, employees missing in payroll, hours on closed cost centres, and flags for collective agreement rules such as minimum call-out pay, double time after scheduled hours and statutory holiday premiums, correcting entries after checking with supervisors.

control.basis: Pay provisions of the company's 11 collective agreements

evidence.note: Double-time overtime and shift and weekend premiums from the IBEW agreement summary; volume of flags is an estimate.

steps.name: Enter employee changes from HR
steps.description: The payroll specialist keys or checks the period's new hires, terminations, transfers, pay rate and step changes, leaves and benefit enrolments received from HR, confirming effective dates against signed offer letters and change forms.

evidence.note: About 60 to 100 changes per run for 1,300 employees, more during the mine wind-down and plant conversions. Estimate.

steps.name: Key one-time payments and deductions
steps.description: The payroll specialist enters bonuses, retention and severance payments, garnishments, union dues changes, savings plan elections and expense reimbursements paid through payroll, each from an approved form.

error.defect_description: Payment keyed twice or to the wrong employee.

next.condition: a collective agreement was settled with retroactive increases

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Calculate retroactive pay after a settlement
steps.description: After a collective agreement is ratified late, the payroll specialist recalculates every affected employee's pay for each past period at the new rates, including overtime and premiums tied to the base rate, checks samples by hand and loads the differences as retroactive earnings.

error.defect_description: Retro calculation misses premiums or overtime tied to the base rate.

control.basis: Retroactive wage terms of the ratified collective agreement

evidence.note: The IBEW Local 254 agreement for 2017-2019 was ratified in January 2018, a year after its term began, so increases had to be paid back to January 2017. With 11 agreements, a few runs a year carry retro pay; share of runs is an estimate.

steps.name: Run preliminary payroll calculation
steps.description: The payroll system calculates gross pay, taxes, CPP and EI, union dues, pension and benefit deductions and net pay for every employee and produces the preliminary register and variance reports.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Review payroll register and variance report
steps.description: The payroll specialist compares each employee's gross and net pay with the previous period, investigates swings above a threshold, negative or zero net pay, missing employees and unusually large overtime, and checks totals by union and cost centre.

error.defect_description: A real error dismissed as an expected change.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Correct errors and recalculate
steps.description: The payroll specialist fixes the time or employee data behind each flagged item, after checking with the supervisor or HR where needed, and reruns the calculation for the affected employees.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Independent review of payroll register
steps.description: A second payroll specialist who did not prepare the run reviews the register totals, the largest payments, new employees' bank details and all one-time payments against their approval forms, and signs the checklist.

control.basis: Payroll preparer and reviewer are different people

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Approve payroll and funding
steps.description: The HR director reviews the register summary, headcount and gross pay against the last run and the budget, asks about large changes and approves the payroll and the funding amount.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: payroll approval by the HR director

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Fund payroll account and approve bank file
steps.description: The treasury analyst moves the net pay amount into the payroll bank account, confirms the total in the direct deposit file matches the approved payroll and approves the file in the bank portal.

control.basis: Payroll funds released by treasury, not payroll

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Transmit direct deposit file to bank
steps.description: The payroll specialist generates the direct deposit file and sends it to the bank by the bank's cut-off two banking days before pay day, then checks the bank's acknowledgement of file total and count.

error.defect_description: File sent late, missing the bank cut-off.

evidence.note: Two-day lead time for direct deposit files is common bank practice in Canada; estimate.

steps.name: Bank deposits net pay on pay day
steps.description: The bank processes the direct deposit file and credits each employee's account on the pay date, which falls within ten days after the pay period ends as Alberta employment standards require.

control.basis: Alberta Employment Standards Code: wages paid within 10 consecutive days after the end of the pay period

evidence.note: The 10-day limit is from the source; the two-day file lead time is an estimate.

steps.name: Publish pay statements in employee self-service
steps.description: The payroll system publishes each employee's statement of earnings online, showing hours, regular and overtime rates, itemised earnings and every deduction, as Alberta employment standards require each pay period.

control.basis: Alberta Employment Standards Code: statement of earnings each pay period

next.condition: employees raise pay errors needing an off-cycle payment

steps.name: Remit source deductions to CRA
steps.description: The payroll specialist totals the income tax, CPP and EI withheld plus the employer's CPP and EI share for the run and pays it to the Canada Revenue Agency through the bank portal before the accelerated remitter due date, the third working day after the remitting period that contains the pay date.

error.defect_description: Late or short remittance attracting a CRA penalty.

control.basis: Income Tax Act source deduction remittance: threshold 2 accelerated remitter due dates

next.condition: monthly union dues and pension remittances due

evidence.note: With about 1,300 employees, withholdings far exceed the 100,000 CAD monthly threshold, so the company is a threshold 2 remitter (author's inference from the source thresholds).

steps.name: Remit union dues and pension contributions
steps.description: Once a month the payroll specialist prepares the union dues listing for each of the bargaining units and the pension contribution file, sends them to the unions and the pension plan administrator and pays the amounts.

error.defect_description: Dues listing omits employees who changed units.

control.basis: Union dues remittance terms of the collective agreements

evidence.note: 11 collective agreements (organisation file) each require a dues listing; monthly timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Post payroll costs to the general ledger
steps.description: The payroll specialist runs the cost distribution that spreads pay and employer costs across cost centres, maintenance work orders and capital or outage projects according to the hours charged, reviews the suspense lines for closed work orders and posts the journal to the ERP.

error.defect_description: Labour charged to closed or wrong work orders.

evidence.note: Labour charged to work orders and capital projects is standard in plant maintenance modules; estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile payroll clearing accounts
steps.description: A controllership accountant reconciles the payroll clearing, withholding and benefit liability accounts to the register and the remittances, clears suspense postings to the right cost objects and signs off the reconciliation.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: account reconciliation and review

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Handle pay queries and issue off-cycle payments
steps.description: The payroll specialist answers employees whose statements show missing overtime, premiums or a wrong rate, checks the approved timesheets, and when the company owes money issues an off-cycle direct deposit or manual cheque rather than waiting for the next run.

error.defect_description: Off-cycle payment duplicates an amount already corrected in the next run.

evidence.note: Shift-premium and overtime errors are the usual cause of off-cycle payments for unionised shift workers; estimate.

exceptions.name: Retroactive pay after a late settlement
exceptions.description: A collective agreement is ratified months after its term began, so every affected employee's past periods are recalculated at the new rates.

exceptions.name: Register corrections
exceptions.description: The variance review finds miscoded premiums, wrong rates or missing employees; data is fixed and the payroll recalculated.

exceptions.name: Off-cycle payments
exceptions.description: Employees report missing overtime or premiums after pay day and receive a separate payment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from pay period end to costs posted and reconciled
benchmarks.population: Biweekly payroll runs at an Alberta employer of about 1,300 staff

evidence.note: Rests on pay day falling about 6 days after period end (Alberta allows at most 10, ab_pay_earnings), CRA remittance within the accelerated remitter window (cra_remit) and GL posting and reconciliation in the following days.

benchmarks.population: Employers under the Alberta Employment Standards Code

benchmarks.unit: working days after each weekly remitting period

pain_points.description: Supervisors on rotating shifts approve time late or not at all, so payroll chases approvals every run.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Shift, weekend, call-out and overtime premiums under several collective agreements are coded by hand and often wrong, causing register corrections and off-cycle payments.

evidence.note: Premium types from the agreement summary; error frequency is an estimate.

pain_points.description: Collective agreements ratified long after their start date force retroactive recalculation of many past periods.

evidence.note: Agreement for 2017-2019 ratified in January 2018.

sources.title: Payment of earnings
sources.supports: Wages must be paid at least monthly and within 10 consecutive days after the end of each pay period; each pay period the employee receives a statement of earnings showing hours, regular and overtime rates, itemised earnings and each deduction; electronic statements are allowed.

sources.title: When to remit (pay) source deductions
sources.supports: Threshold 2 accelerated remitters (average monthly withholding of 100,000 CAD or more two years earlier) remit up to four times a month, for the 1st-7th, 8th-14th, 15th-21st and 22nd-end of month, each due the third working day after the period ends.

sources.title: TransAlta Generation Partnership and IBEW Local 254 collective agreement summary
sources.supports: Agreement covering 285 production employees, term January 1, 2017 to December 31, 2019, ratified January 22, 2018 and signed March 23, 2018, more than a year after the term began; 3.3 percent increase; evening and night shift premium 2.79 CAD per hour rising to 2.84; weekend premium of one hour's pay for maintenance staff and hydro operator-maintainers; overtime at double time.

assumptions: Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Supervisor time approval is shown as one step with the combined time of about 60 supervisors; because they work in parallel, the simulated cycle time overstates elapsed time by up to a day.
Payroll specialist fte_on_process covers only work on the run; benefits, pension, year-end, records of employment and enquiries outside the run are other processes.
Pay day is assumed to be the Friday after a period ending on Saturday or Sunday, inside the 10-day limit.
The pension plan administrator receives contributions but is not an external party in the organisation file, so only the union remittance is listed in interfaces.

Validator check: simulated median cycle time is about 11.4 days (p90 14) against the tier C benchmark of 9; pay day is reached after a median of about 6.8 days, inside the 10-day legal limit. The gap to the benchmark comes from the supervisors' combined approval time counted serially (about 20 hours) and from off-cycle payments in half the runs.

Staffing check: roles state 2.5 FTE while hands-on time implies about 1.0 FTE. The stated payroll specialist time includes run-related work the steps do not itemise (answering supervisor questions during the run, preparing audit and union reports, checking garnishment and benefit setups), so the gap is left rather than inflating step times that would lengthen the simulated cycle.
